critical_code_review_comments: scheduler._nightly_job: win-back email loop (2b) and lapsed-downgrade update_many (2c) run in separate DB round-trips. Under a concurrent scheduler run the same user could get counted twice for the winback IF winback_sent_for is not yet set — mitigated in practice by winback_sent_for check, but the downgrade update_many is unconditional (matches on subscription_expires < now regardless of winback_sent_for). If a fast concurrent worker triggered downgrade first, the second worker's 2b loop would already see subscription_tier='free' and skip winback. Order is correct here (winback runs before downgrade), but a comment noting that invariant would help future refactors.

community_router.founding_partners: `.to_list(20)` caps to 20 but max cohort is 10 (5 global + 5 seattle). Fine, but the field-level projection here differs from list_partners (no user_id/bio) — intentional but inconsistent; consider a shared helper for the projection.

RenewalReminder.jsx: `daysLeft` uses `Math.ceil` — a 30-day expiry evaluated at 23:59 could evaluate to 31 days ceil'd. The check `left > 30` will hide the banner on the final second before rollover; acceptable but note the boundary.

mobile app/clubs.tsx: cards without a handle become no-op (`onPress={() => item.handle && router.push(...)}`) — safe, but there is no visual hint. Consider disabling pressable/opacity when handle is falsy.

GET /api/partners: no explicit rate limit or authentication. Directory is public which is fine, but a curl bomb could scrape the full org list. Consider a lightweight IP-based limit for parity with other public endpoints.
